clue.text: Great story that's a delight for the backward reader

indicators.note: a reader going backward takes the phrase from its end to its start

parts.note: a gas is informal for something hugely enjoyable

explanation.surface: A bookworm praises a long tale that pleases even someone reading it back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the backward reader' turns the whole of A GAS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A long heroic narrative, such as the Icelandic family epics, is the classic example of a great story.

clue.text: The arrogance (not imaginary) of stars

parts.note: side is an old British word for swagger or pretentiousness, as in 'no side about him'
something not imaginary is actual

explanation.surface: A remark about the haughtiness of celebrities, which the writer insists is no fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' looks like celebrities; it is astronomy. 'Side' for conceit is chiefly British.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things measured against the fixed stars, as in astronomical time.

clue.text: Create scale for qualified person

definitions.meaning: to mark a vessel or ruler with divisions of measure
someone who holds a university degree

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to mark off in degrees; as a noun, someone who has completed a degree.

clue.text: Seals experience a narrow escape

parts.note: to seal something is to shut it
to have a bad time is to experience one

explanation.surface: Seals out on the ice have a lucky escape from danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seals' looks like the animals; it is the verb meaning shuts.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from the barber's chair for something that very nearly went wrong.

clue.text: Sponge in a dessert used up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are written from bottom to top

parts.note: a fool is a pudding of fruit puree folded into cream

explanation.surface: A sponge cake has been put into a pudding and eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used up' sounds like eaten, but in a down clue it turns A FOOL round.
explanation.definitionFit: The dried fibrous pod of a gourd is used as a bath scrubber, a kind of sponge.

clue.text: Boats sure to blow up destroyers

indicators.note: blowing things up scatters them, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Saboteurs are sure to blow up the boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyers' looks like warships, fitting the boats; it means wreckers.
explanation.definitionFit: People who deliberately wreck equipment or plans are wreckers of property.

clue.text: One who arranges flats and properties

definitions.text: One who arranges flats and properties

parts.words: One who arranges flats and properties
parts.note: reads as an estate agent, but flats are painted canvas scenery panels and properties the stage props that a theatre hand moves between scenes

explanation.definitionFit: A stagehand moves scenery panels and props during a play's changes of scene.

clue.text: North American father's in pain

indicators.note: the father is placed inside the word for pain

parts.note: an ache is a dull pain
pa is an informal word for father; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A man's dad is suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a Native American people of the south-western United States.

clue.text: Succeed, securing right to guarantee

indicators.note: the word for succeed holds the abbreviation fast inside it

parts.note: to succeed, follow on after, is to ensue

explanation.surface: Advice to win by getting a legal right that underwrites your position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeed' looks like win; here it means follow after.
explanation.definitionFit: To make certain of an outcome is to guarantee it.

clue.text: Hand out cards to do business

definitions.meaning: to distribute the cards to players
to trade, as in '... in antiques'

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both distributing playing cards and trading with someone.

clue.text: No single bed, we hear, will do -for this player

indicators.note: signals that the words should be sounded out rather than spelt

parts.note: a bed that is not a single is a double, and a divan bed stands on a base

explanation.surface: Someone sleeping alone says a large bed is not needed and the player can have it.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed base of a double divan sounds the same as the bass instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest bowed string instrument of the orchestra, and by extension the musician playing it.

clue.text: All-inclusive price of ticket for the highway

parts.note: something thorough leaves nothing out
a fare is the price paid for a journey

explanation.surface: A traveller asks the full cost of a ticket for travel on the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A main road open to traffic at both ends is a public highway.

clue.text: Boisterous actors get plastered

parts.note: rough play is boisterous play
the cast is the set of actors in a production

explanation.surface: Rowdy actors go out and get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastered' looks like drunk; it means coated with plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall coated in coarse plaster mixed with gravel has been rendered this way.

clue.text: Number of surgery patients heavens above!

definitions.meaning: a numb-er, something that numbs, as the old anaesthetic did
the clear upper sky, in poetic usage

explanation.definitionFit: The volatile liquid was an early anaesthetic, and the poetic word names the upper regions of the sky.

clue.text: Rafter, though thick, needs this bit added later

indicators.note: the clue words need, or contain, the run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A carpenter says a beam, though thick, still needs an extra piece fitted on later.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'Rafter, though thick' from the A to the first T of thick.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thought of only once the main work is done is a later addition.

clue.text: How to convert coop to store, for example

definitions.text: How to convert coop to store, for example

parts.words: How to convert coop to store, for example
parts.note: putting a short dash into the hen-house word turns it into co-op, a cooperative shop

explanation.definitionFit: To join or split word parts with a short dash, as co-op is written.

clue.text: Policemen in uniform attached to sections of the Yard

parts.note: a flat rate is a uniform one
a yard divides into three feet

explanation.surface: Uniformed officers are posted to departments of Scotland Yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Yard' suggests Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters; it is the unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang term for police officers, from the patrolling constable's supposedly fallen arches.

clue.text: Print company unable to get various parts

parts.note: type is printed lettering
a cast is a company of actors

explanation.surface: A printing firm cannot obtain assorted spare components.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor confined to one kind of role cannot win a range of other roles.

clue.text: Supply fuel or components with a definite aim in mind .

definitions.text: with a definite aim in mind

indicators.note: the letters are treated as parts to be assembled into a new whole

explanation.surface: Fuel or spare parts are delivered with a clear goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting deliberately and with intent is acting toward a set aim.

clue.text: Emerged from second crash

parts.note: a prang is British slang for a minor car crash

explanation.surface: A driver walked out of a minor collision.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring from somewhere is to emerge or arise from it.

clue.text: It's too much, denying one opportunity to rise

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters are written upward, so reversed
the word for one is refused a place, so it is taken out

parts.note: unity is the number one

explanation.surface: Someone complains it is unfair to deny a person the chance to get on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'denying' takes the word for one out of the clue word, and 'to rise' turns what remains upward; 'It's' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian musical direction, as in non troppo, meaning excessively.

clue.text: Rod for getting fish

definitions.meaning: an old measure of length, five and a half yards, also called a pole

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an old unit of land measure equal to a rod and a common river fish.

clue.text: Holy church cutting short right of admission in middle of upheaval

indicators.note: the holy church letters are placed within the shortened word
the right of admission loses its final letter

parts.note: entree is the right to enter a place
pi is schoolboy slang for pious
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A holy church limiting entry stands at the heart of a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting short' docks the last letter of the admission word, and 'in' sets the holy church letters just after its opening letter. Pi for pious is old British school slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The point on the surface above an earthquake's origin is the centre of the shaking.

clue.text: I see you are talking about new contract

indicators.note: the sounded letters go around the abbreviation for new
the words are said aloud and written as the letters they sound like

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like ICUR

explanation.surface: Someone says they gather the other person is discussing a fresh agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I see you are' spoken is the letters I C U R, text-message style.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract a debt or an illness is to bring it on oneself.

clue.text: Showing up pretence

definitions.meaning: an outward show that may be false

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means both turning up somewhere and a false outward impression.

clue.text: Girl in port abandoning so-called cruise

indicators.note: the port drops the part that sounds like the voyage

parts.note: Veracruz is a major Mexican port on the Gulf

indicators.note: signals that the word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a cruise is a pleasure voyage

explanation.surface: A woman in a harbour town gives up her planned sea holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spanish CRUZ sounds like cruise.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, as with the wartime singer Lynn.

clue.text: Unwanted third person may be made a fool of

definitions.meaning: someone tagging along with a courting couple

definitions.text: may be made a fool of
definitions.meaning: a fruit often made into a fool, a creamy dessert

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an unwanted chaperone; the tart green berry goes into a classic British cream pudding.

clue.text: Reinstate Test broadcast

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters something widely, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bring back the cricket Test on air.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A proofreader's mark meaning let it stand, restoring a deleted passage.
